In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PKC-α, -δ, and -η are required for TNF-α-stimulated translocation of n-SMase2 to the plasma membrane, and this is a key regulatory event in TNF-α-induced signaling in lung epithelial cells.

PKC-α and -δ are required for TNF-α-induced nSMase2 activation and nSMase-dependent adhesion molecule expression in A549 cells, but PKC-δ is the only PKC isoform that is required for TNFα-induced translocation of the nSMase2 enzyme to the plasma membrane.
PKC-Δ is a novel regulator of nSMases in the lung epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNF-α induces nSMase2 to the PM via p38 and PKCδ in a sequential manner.
TNF stimulates N-SMase2 translocation through p38 and PKC-α, and PKC-β1 and PKC-ε are not involved in this process.

PKC-α/β, PKC-ε, PKC-η, and PKC-ι are involved in TNF-stimulating p38 MAPK and N-SMase activities, whereas PKC-δ is involved in TNF-induced N-sSMase2 translocalization and subsequent induction of vascular cell adhesion molecule 1 and intercellular cell adhesion molecule-1.
